params.name: obstacle
params.label: Obstacle
params.help: What to drop into the stream — a shape, a vehicle, or your own text.

params.name: text
params.label: Your text
params.help: The word to drop into the stream. Short words read best.

params.name: size
params.label: Obstacle size
params.help: Obstacle size (cylinder diameter, square side, airfoil chord/2.6) as a fraction of the channel height. Bigger → larger, slower-shedding wake.
params.fixed: Re is held: ν is recomputed from the new D

params.name: angle
params.label: Airfoil angle of attack
params.help: Angle of attack in degrees; positive = leading edge up (lift upward). Negative angles mirror the flow and give downward lift.

params.name: reynolds
params.label: Reynolds number
params.help: Reynolds number Re = U·D/ν (inertia ÷ viscosity) with D the reference length below. Low → smooth steady flow; high → vortex shedding and turbulence.
params.fixed: U and D stay; ν = U·D/Re changes

params.name: speed
params.label: Inflow speed
params.help: Inlet flow speed in lattice units. The Reynolds number is held fixed: the viscosity is recomputed as ν = U·D/Re, so a higher speed means a higher lattice Mach number (keep ≲ 0.15) and a shorter physical time per step, not a stronger wake.
params.fixed: Re stays; ν changes with U

params.name: xpos
params.label: Obstacle position
params.help: Streamwise position of the obstacle centre as a fraction of the tunnel length.

params.name: resolution
params.label: Resolution
params.help: Grid resolution. It changes the grid, and with it whatever a scene ties to the grid: the elapsed convective time in the wind tunnel, the Rayleigh number in the convection scenes, the grain size in the rock, the extent of the blast box. The derived readouts say what moved for this experiment; runs at different resolutions are comparable only where they say so.

params.name: duration
params.label: Duration (×)
params.help: Simulated interval as a multiple of the scene's reference interval (1.0 = default).

params.name: buoyancy
params.label: Buoyancy coefficient
params.help: Buoyancy coefficient: force per unit of the transported scalar (dye/temperature). Higher → a faster, more vigorous plume.

params.name: confinement
params.label: Vorticity confinement
params.help: Vorticity confinement — re-injects small-scale swirl lost to numerical diffusion (a modelling knob, not a physical property). 0 = none.

params.name: viscosity
params.label: Viscosity
params.help: Kinematic viscosity ν — how 'thick' the fluid is. Lower → finer, more chaotic structures; higher → smoother, damped flow.

params.name: flicker
params.label: Source flicker
params.help: Wobble & pulse the source (a prescribed modulation of the inflow, not a physical instability). 0 = a steady column; 1 = a lively, flame-like pulse.

params.name: source
params.label: Source width
params.help: Width of the hot source at the floor.

params.name: buoyancy
params.label: Heat-release buoyancy
params.help: How strongly the temperature proxy T(Z) lifts the gas. Stronger buoyancy draws the fuel up faster, keeping the flame slender and steady.

params.name: zst
params.label: Stoichiometric mixture  Z_st
params.help: The fuel/air ratio at which the flame sheet sits. The luminous sheet is the Z = Z_st surface; a larger value pulls it tighter to the fuel core.

params.name: source
params.label: Wick width
params.help: Width of the fuel vapour leaving the wick. A thin wick gives a slender flame.

params.name: confinement
params.label: Vorticity confinement
params.help: Sharpens the small eddies that make the flame tip lick and wander (a modelling knob).

params.name: atwood
params.label: Atwood number
params.help: A = (ρ_heavy − ρ_light)/(ρ_heavy + ρ_light), the density contrast across the interface. Higher A → faster, narrower spikes. (Boussinesq-like model: density only enters the buoyancy force; see the scene notes.)

params.name: gravity
params.label: Gravity
params.help: Gravity driving the instability. Higher → faster fingering / collapse.

params.name: viscosity
params.label: Viscosity
params.help: Kinematic viscosity ν — how 'thick' the fluid is. Lower → finer, more chaotic structures; higher → smoother, damped flow.

params.name: perturbation
params.label: Interface ripple
params.help: Amplitude of the initial interface ripple that seeds the fingers.

params.name: modes
params.label: Single-mode wavenumber
params.help: 0 = the multi-mode ripple (modes 3 + 7). A value n ≥ 1 seeds a single cosine mode with n wavelengths across the box and a small amplitude, for measuring the early growth of one mode.

params.name: buoyancy
params.label: Buoyancy coefficient  β·ΔT
params.help: Buoyant acceleration per unit temperature difference. With the viscosity and thermal diffusivity it sets the Rayleigh number Ra = β·ΔT·H³/(ν κ) shown in the derived quantities — this control is NOT itself a Rayleigh number. 0 = pure conduction.

params.name: viscosity
params.label: Viscosity ν
params.help: Damps the motion. Lower viscosity → a higher Rayleigh number → tighter, more chaotic cells.

params.name: kappa
params.label: Thermal diffusivity κ
params.help: Conduction of heat. Together with ν it sets the Prandtl number ν/κ and the Rayleigh number. (Explicit diffusion step: κ·dt must stay ≤ 0.25.)

params.name: perturbation
params.label: Seed ripple
params.help: Amplitude of the tiny temperature perturbation that breaks the symmetry and selects the cell wavelength.

exhibits.name: Detonation

params.name: scene
params.label: Scene
params.help: Open air: a free blast wave expanding into still gas. Shock hits a city: a ground burst whose blast diffracts around and reflects off two solid towers.

params.name: pressure
params.label: Charge pressure ratio  p₀ / p_ambient
params.help: Pressure inside the charge relative to the ambient pressure (0.1 in code units). Higher → a stronger, faster shock. The solver receives p₀ = ratio × 0.1.

params.name: charge
params.label: Charge size
params.help: Radius of the high-pressure charge as a fraction of the domain width.

params.name: structure
params.label: Structure model
params.help: Rigid walls: the towers are fixed reflecting obstacles. Erodes: an experimental rule removes a block when the overpressure on an exposed face exceeds its strength (not a structural-mechanics model).

params.name: strength
params.label: Structure strength
params.help: Overpressure each block can take before it fails (erosion model only). Weak structures are scoured away windward-first.

params.name: debris
params.label: Debris particles
params.help: Glowing debris swept outward by the blast (visual only; not part of the solution).

exhibits.method: Blast wave (pressure release) · Compressible Euler · finite-volume HLLC

params.name: resolution
params.label: Resolution
params.help: Cells along the tube (the tube is one-dimensional; the strip is for display). Higher resolution sharpens the shock and contact discontinuity.

params.name: duration
params.label: Duration (×)
params.help: Fraction of the reference time 0.2 (tube length 1); at 1.0 the waves have not yet reached the ends.

params.name: target
params.label: Target
params.help: One gas bubble, or two stacked bubbles whose roll-ups interact.

params.name: mach
params.label: Shock Mach number
params.help: Strength of the incoming shock, M_s = (shock speed)/(sound speed). The post-shock state follows the exact Rankine–Hugoniot relations (see derived quantities).

params.name: densratio
params.label: Density ratio ρ_bubble/ρ_air
params.help: Bubble density ÷ ambient density. <1 = a light bubble (rolls up fast); >1 = a heavy bubble (the shock slows and focuses inside it).

params.name: bubble
params.label: Bubble size
params.help: Bubble radius as a fraction of the domain height.

params.label: Resolution
params.help: Grid resolution. It changes the grid, and with it whatever a scene ties to the grid: the elapsed convective time in the wind tunnel, the Rayleigh number in the convection scenes, the grain size in the rock, the extent of the blast box. params.name: duration
params.label: Duration (×)
params.help: Simulated interval as a multiple of the scene's reference interval (1.0 = default).

params.name: scene
params.label: Scene
params.help: Which free-surface scenario to run. Each scene exposes its own controls below. Still water is the hydrostatic baseline: nothing should move.

params.name: width
params.label: Dam width
params.help: Width of the held-back water column (tank 5 × 3.2 m).

params.name: height
params.label: Dam height
params.help: Height of the column — more head → a faster, taller surge.

params.name: dropsize
params.label: Blob diameter
params.help: Diameter of the falling water blob (a parcel of water, not a capillary droplet — there is no surface tension in this model).

params.name: dropheight
params.label: Release height
params.help: How high the blob starts, as a fraction of tank height (sets the impact speed √(2 g h)).

params.name: sloshA
params.label: Slosh strength
params.help: Amplitude of the oscillating sideways gravity, as a multiple of g.

params.name: sloshT
params.label: Slosh period
params.help: Period of the side-to-side forcing. Near the tank's natural period the wave resonates and breaks.

params.name: spout
params.label: Spout width
params.help: Half-width of the pour stream as a fraction of the glass width. Values below 3 particle spacings are raised to that minimum (shown in derived quantities).

params.name: pourv
params.label: Pour speed
params.help: Speed the water leaves the spout. Faster → more splashing on impact.

params.name: waveA
params.label: Wavemaker stroke
params.help: Stroke of the wavemaker paddle (the wall's travel), which sets the wave amplitude indirectly — it is not the wave height itself. 0 = still paddle (free decay / equilibrium test for the ship).

params.name: waveT
params.label: Wave period
params.help: Period of the wavemaker — sets the wavelength of the train.

params.name: shipsz
params.label: Ship size
params.help: Scale of the floating hull. Bigger ships sit deeper and roll slower.

params.name: particles
params.label: Particles (≈)
params.help: Approximate number of SPH particles: sets the particle spacing dp (see derived quantities). More → finer splash, slower. The pour scene emits particles continuously and ignores this.

params.name: gravity
params.label: Gravity
params.help: Gravitational acceleration.

params.name: duration
params.label: Duration (×)
params.help: Simulated interval as a multiple of the scene's reference interval (1.0 = default).

params.name: init
params.label: Initial field
params.help: Shear layers roll into Kelvin–Helmholtz billows; random turbulence decays as vortices merge (the 2-D inverse cascade); the Taylor–Green vortex is an exact decaying solution (energy ∝ exp(−4νt)) used to check the solver.

params.name: viscosity
params.label: Viscosity ν
params.help: Kinematic viscosity ν — how 'thick' the fluid is. Lower → finer, more chaotic structures; higher → smoother, damped flow.

params.name: perturbation
params.label: Shear perturbation
params.help: Amplitude of the initial transverse velocity kick that seeds the billows.

params.name: thickness
params.label: Shear-layer thickness
params.help: Thickness of each tanh shear layer as a fraction of the box size L.

params.name: seed
params.label: Random seed
params.help: Seed of the random initial vorticity (same seed → same experiment).

params.name: duration
params.label: Duration (×)
params.help: Simulated interval as a multiple of the scene's reference interval (1.0 = default).

params.name: porosity
params.label: Porosity φ
params.help: Fraction of the sample that is pore space. The same rock as the porous-flow experiment: with the same porosity, grain size and seed you get the same sample.

params.name: grain
params.label: Grain size
params.help: Typical grain radius as a fraction of the sample height. It also sets the length in the Péclet number.

params.name: seed
params.label: Sample seed
params.help: Which random grain arrangement to pack. Same seed, same rock.

params.name: direction
params.label: Driving direction
params.help: Which way the flow (and the tracer) is driven.

params.name: strength
params.label: Driving strength
params.help: Body force driving the flow, as a multiple of the default. In the Darcy regime it changes the speed but not the permeability; with the Péclet number held, it does not change the spreading either.
params.fixed: Pe is held: the molecular diffusivity is rescaled with the pore speed

params.name: peclet
params.label: Péclet number
params.help: How strongly the tracer is carried compared with how fast it spreads: Pe = u·d/D_m with u the pore speed and d the grain size. Below 1 diffusion dominates and the plume stays symmetric; above about 10 fast and slow channels stretch it and the breakthrough curve grows a long tail.
params.fixed: the molecular diffusivity follows from Pe and the measured pore speed

params.name: injection
params.label: Injection
params.help: A continuous supply holds the inlet at full concentration and sends a front through the sample; the outlet curve climbs towards 1. A pulse releases one slug instead, which passes and leaves, giving a curve that rises, peaks and decays.

params.name: F
params.label: Feed rate F
params.help: Rate at which U is fed in (and V removed with k).

params.name: k
params.label: Removal rate k
params.help: Rate at which V is removed.

params.name: Du
params.label: Diffusivity of U
params.help: Diffusion coefficient of U (explicit scheme: keep Du ≤ 0.25 for stability at dt = 1).

params.name: Dv
params.label: Diffusivity of V
params.help: Diffusion coefficient of V. Patterns need Dv < Du (Turing's condition).
